vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: xiaodi-obsidian-brain-pro
Version: 1.1.3

The skill bundle is a productivity tool designed to sync Obsidian notes via Git and provide local semantic search using Ollama. It demonstrates a strong security posture by including explicit 'Red Line' rules in its system prompts (prompts/organizer.txt and prompts/system_prompt_v2.txt) that instruct the AI to automatically redact sensitive information such as API keys, passwords, and tokens before storage or transmission. While the scripts (scripts/sync.sh and scripts/push_to_git.sh) perform broad Git operations and search_engine.py contains a hardcoded local IP (192.168.3.120), these appear to be functional requirements or development oversights rather than malicious intent, and the documentation consistently emphasizes user privacy and local-first processing.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (local Obsidian ingestion + local Ollama search + privacy-first Git backup) mostly matches its files, but there are important mismatches and omissions — in particular the promised automatic privacy desensitization is not implemented in the delivered scripts, and runtime env vars/defaults are undeclared and potentially dangerous (hardcoded network default + blind git push).

dimensions.detail: The name/description (WhatsApp/Telegram → Obsidian, local Ollama embeddings, privacy desensitization, optional Git backup) aligns with the included files: templates/prompts for formatting, a search_engine.py that calls Ollama, and git push scripts. However the skill promises automatic privacy redaction and 'API Key/Token replacement' before pushing to GitHub, but there is no code in the repository that performs the regex-based redaction or sanitization prior to commit/push — the push scripts add and commit everything in the Obsidian directory. That is a substantive mismatch between claimed capability and actual implementation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and prompts instruct the agent to read user notes, transform/format them, and run Git push scripts. The runtime code will read Markdown files under user Obsidian paths and push them to a remote via git. The instructions require the agent to access local file paths and execute shell scripts (exec), which is expected for this purpose — but they grant the agent authority to push the entire vault and rely on a promised redaction step that is specified only in prompts/spec but not implemented in code. The skill also references env vars (OLLAMA_BASE_URL etc.) and paths not declared in requires.env, so the runtime behavior depends on externally set variables that aren't surfaced in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only skill) and included scripts are small, plain shell/Python files. There are no downloads of arbitrary archives or network installers. Risk from installation is low; runtime risk comes from executing the provided scripts (git push, network calls) rather than from an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared metadata lists no required env vars, but the Python and shell scripts use/expect: OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL, OBSIDIAN_DIR (or default ~/Obsidian), REMOTE_REPO, REMOTE_BRANCH. Those are not declared as required. The skill will attempt network access to the Ollama endpoint (default: http://192.168.3.120:11434) — a hardcoded LAN IP that looks like a developer/test default — and will run git push which relies on the user's git credentials but does not declare or request them. The absence of explicit credential requirements combined with the scripts' behavior is a proportionality mismatch and a safety concern.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (normal). _meta.json requests file_read/file_write/exec permissions which are coherent for a note-ingestion + sync skill. The skill does not request global 'always' privilege or attempt to modify other skills. However the ability to read/write the vault and run git push gives it significant ability to exfiltrate data if misconfigured, so the user should treat those permissions carefully.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key points to consider before installing/running this skill:

1) Privacy vs implementation gap: The README/SKILL.md repeatedly promises automatic redaction of API keys/tokens/passwords. I could not find code that actually performs that redaction before files are committed/pushed; the provided git scripts add and push the entire vault as-is. Do not assume your secrets are being sanitized — review or implement a pre-commit redaction step before using remote backups.

2) Git pushes can leak notes: The push/sync scripts will run git add/commit/push on the configured Obsidian directory. Make sure the configured remote is correct and private, and manually verify the set of files to be pushed. Consider testing in an isolated vault (no sensitive data) first.

3) Undeclared env vars and dangerous defaults: search_engine.py defaults OLLAMA_BASE_URL to http://192.168.3.120:11434 (a developer LAN IP). Confirm OLLAMA_BASE_URL points to your own local Ollama instance. Also set OBSIDIAN_DIR and git remote vars explicitly rather than relying on defaults.

4) Confirm redaction logic or add controls: If you want automatic redaction, either obtain/inspect the code that performs it or add a pre-push sanitizer (a script that applies robust regex checks and refuses to push when secrets are present). The prompts describe detection heuristics, but those are not a substitute for implemented code.

5) Run in a sandbox first: Install and run in a test environment (separate vault) and watch exactly what gets committed/pushed. Inspect commit contents and the output of the scripts before enabling automatic scheduled agents.

6) If you need higher assurance: ask the maintainer to (a) implement/point to the actual redaction routine, (b) remove hardcoded network defaults, (c) declare required env vars and document how credentials are provided. Presence of these changes would materially reduce the concerns noted above.

What would change my assessment to 'benign': visible, implemented redaction code executed before any git commit/push; removal of hardcoded OLLAMA_BASE_URL (or safe default localhost); explicit declares of the env vars/credentials required; and tests/logs demonstrating no sensitive data is pushed.
